chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Yusuf ibn al-Harith, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azrami, from his father, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them: “It was established concerning...”

For the blackened tooth, one-third of its diyah; for the paralyzed hand, one-third of its diyah; for the standing eye when its sight is effaced, one-third of its diyah; for the earlobe, one-third of its diyah; for the lame leg, one-third of its diyah; and for the soft parts of the nose, in each one there is one-third of the diyah.”

key_terms.الْعَيْنِ الْقَائِمَةِ: an eye that remains physically present
key_terms.خِشَاشِ الْأَنْفِ: the soft inner or delicate parts of the nose
key_terms.شَحْمَةِ الْأُذُنِ: the fleshy lower part of the ear, i.e. the earlobe
key_terms.طَمَسَتْ: its sight was effaced or obliterated

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for injuring a paralyzed hand, blackened tooth, damaged eye, earlobe, lame leg, or parts of the nose in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states fixed legal compensations for injuries to certain bodily organs and defective limbs. It belongs to the jurisprudence of diyah, specifying that these listed injuries carry one-third of the full prescribed compensation.
